easy.q: What name does President Farnes give to the moments when God places someone in our path and we see them?
options: Divine appointments
Quiet miracles
Sacred errands
easy.why: President Farnes said ministering often happens when God places someone in our path and we have eyes to see them. He calls these moments “divine appointments.”

easy.q: President Farnes walked into the temple feeling discouraged. Who asked him, “How are you, brother?”
options: His stake president
Elder Dallin H. Oaks
The temple president
easy.why: It was Elder Dallin H. Oaks, whom President Farnes had never met. Elder Oaks then waited for him, listened, and encouraged him.

easy.q: After a hard meeting, President Farnes did not want to go to ward temple night. What did he ask his wife to do instead?
options: Stay home and rest
Take the children to a park
Go to dinner
easy.why: He said, “Let’s go to dinner instead of the temple.” His wife, Linsey, wisely answered that he needed to be in the temple, and that is where his help came.

easy.q: At the airport, a frightened young missionary was holding his boarding pass and one other thing. What was it?
options: A digital alarm clock
A letter from his mother
A map of the airport
easy.why: “Clutched in his hands were his boarding pass and a digital alarm clock.” He held the clock to make sure he did not miss the plane.

easy.q: What did President Farnes invite us to pray for every day?
options: A calmer day with fewer interruptions
Courage to speak up in Church meetings
Eyes to see the people God puts before us
easy.why: He said, “let us pray every day for eyes to see the divine appointments God places before us!” Then we put compassion into action for the person in front of us.

medium.q: Elder Oaks told President Farnes, “But it’s what we do. Isn’t it?” According to President Farnes, what is it that “we do”?
options: Keep a full day of Church meetings without complaint
Minister with compassion to whomever God places in our path
Give careful answers to questions in leadership meetings
Remember the name and story of each person we have served
medium.why: President Farnes explained that covenant followers of Jesus Christ minister with compassion to whomever God places in their path, “because that’s what the Savior did.”

medium.q: In this talk, what does it mean to be willing to take upon ourselves the name of Jesus Christ?
options: We promise to accept every calling that is extended to us
We speak His name often in our everyday conversations
We choose to see as He sees, feel as He feels, and do as He would
We commit never to feel discouraged while serving Him
medium.why: President Farnes taught that “we choose to see as He sees, feel as He feels, and do as He would do,” so that people who meet us experience something of Jesus Christ.

medium.q: How does President Farnes connect the sacrament with ministering?
options: We make the covenant on Sunday and keep it by ministering every day
We minister through the week so we can be ready for the sacrament
We are shown whom to minister to while the sacrament is passed
We minister best on Sunday, when sacred time has been set apart
medium.why: He taught that we make the covenant “during sacred time with God every Sunday,” and that a way we keep it is by ministering to God’s children every day.

medium.q: Jesus told of a traveler who lay wounded on the road to Jericho. According to President Farnes, what set apart the one man who helped?
options: He had more time and means than the others on the road
He already knew the traveler and felt a duty to him
He was the only one who passed close enough to notice
He saw a chance to minister where others saw an interruption
medium.why: President Farnes called him “a man who had eyes to see.” Where others saw an inconvenience or an interruption, he saw an opportunity to minister.

medium.q: The frightened missionary boarded last and took the only empty seat, right beside President Farnes. What did the two of them see in that?
options: That the airline had noticed the elder needed help
That God had arranged even a small detail like that one
That missionaries ought to board their flights early
That the Farneses should have waited for him at the gate
medium.why: They smiled at each other, “amazed at how God had arranged even a small detail like that one.” Then the elder finally relaxed and fell asleep.

hard.q: According to President Farnes, what makes it possible for us to minister as the Savior would, with His power and loving kindness?
options: Long experience in Church leadership callings
A naturally warm and outgoing personality
The promised gift of always having His Spirit
A specific assignment from priesthood leaders
hard.why: Our promise of willingness in the sacrament is met by the Lord’s promise that we can always have His Spirit. “With that gift, we can minister as the Savior would.”

hard.q: How does President Farnes say Jesus regarded the people He met in ordinary encounters?
options: They were His mission, not interruptions to it
They were welcome rests from His mission
They were preparation for His later mission
They were tests of patience during His mission
hard.why: President Farnes taught, “To Jesus, these people were not interrupting His mission. They were His mission.” He turned ordinary encounters into moments of healing.

hard.q: Which situation best fits all that President Farnes says turns an ordinary encounter into a “divine appointment”?
options: You notice a new neighbor struggling, feel for him, and plan to help someday
You notice a new neighbor struggling and wonder what he did to cause it
You hear a new neighbor is struggling and assume someone else will step in
You notice a new neighbor struggling, feel for him, and stop to help
hard.why: He said all it took was to “see the person God had placed in our path, look with compassion rather than judgment, and then act.” Seeing without compassion, or compassion without action, stops short.

hard.q: President Farnes saw the anxious missionary and then returned to his book. What changed that glance into a divine appointment?
options: His wife pointed out that the elder was alone
The Spirit prompted him to look again, and he acted
The elder walked over and asked him for help
An airline worker asked him to watch over the elder
hard.why: He first imagined reasons the elder looked anxious and went back to reading. “But the Spirit prompted me to look again,” and this time he asked, “Are you OK?”

hard.q: Looking back on helping the missionary, what does President Farnes say it required of him and his wife?
options: A sacrifice: giving up the vacation they had needed
Courage: approaching a stranger who was in distress
Not much: only to see, look with compassion, and act
Experience: knowing how new missionaries are received
hard.why: He said it “didn’t require much of us.” All they had to do was see the person God placed in their path, “look with compassion rather than judgment, and then act.”
